findings.reason: the plan should carry the four evidence fields onto budget's hold and delete the parallel module, or name the seam that justifies a second hold owner.
findings.text: crew/hold.py builds a second hold (`hold_from_position`, `MissingHoldEvidenceError`) while reckon/budget.py already owns the dispatch hold: `budget.pace_hold` (reckon/budget.py:2588) is the hold the preflight emits into `entry["pace_hold"]`, `budget.withheld_reserves` (reckon/budget.py:238) names the reserve a hold rests on, and `record_hold_checks` (reckon/budget.py:1405) writes it; `crew/hold.py` has no caller anywhere in the tree.

findings.reason: the plan says the shelf life is shared "so the two never disagree" yet records a live disagreement; one owner must supply the horizon.
findings.text: the horizon that decides when a reading stops being a position is owned twice: `staleness.configured_shelf_life_minutes` reads budget.evidence_shelf_life_minutes, while `budget._published_fresh_windows` (reckon/budget.py:1493) ages each backend against `paid_lanes.DEFAULT_STALE_SECONDS` (reckon/crew/paid_lanes.py:62); the plan's own §5b records that the two horizons disagree (47 min vs 60 min) and leaves the disagreement standing.

findings.reason: an unwireable thin wrapper is the design either to fold into the fence's hold or to prescribe the wiring for; both are decisions the plan has not taken.
findings.text: `hold_from_position` forwards to `staleness.resolve_configured_*` and reads a `budget_group.GroupPosition`, contributing only a `used_percent >= ceiling` test and evidence-field checks over machinery `budget.pace_hold` already produces (allowance, utilisation, burn, resets); the plan gives no reason the fence's hold cannot be extended, and its own §7 records that the module's `source` field means "pool" here while evidence rows mean "provenance kind", so a consumer passing a row straight through would refuse every real hold as borrowed.

findings.reason: naming the owner forces the extend-or-fork decision the two modules currently leave implicit.
findings.text: the reuse map is good for the derived figures but the plan did not run it over the hold and staleness seams: §7 built a hold module beside budget.pace_hold, and §5b built a staleness module beside budget._published_fresh_windows, each without a sentence saying why the existing owner was not extended.

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface surface it adds, per the one-rule this item holds against all four families.
findings.text: §6 adds a CLI option (`--ready NAME=GROUP:SCORE`) and §7 adds a refusal family (`MissingHoldEvidenceError`), and neither the section text nor the landing records name an option or family retired or merged, or state why nothing can be.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one call hides the wallet's whole pace position: budget.group_pace and budget_group.group_figures delegate fill, allowance, bar and reserve to pace.py, bar.py and reserve.py behind a single group-keyed entry point, so a caller composes one interface, not six.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — crew/hold.py duplicates the dispatch hold whose owner is reckon/budget.py (pace_hold + withheld_reserves + record_hold_checks), and crew/staleness.py duplicates the freshness horizon whose owner is reckon/paid_lanes.py / reckon/budget.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §6 adds the `--ready NAME=GROUP:SCORE` CLI option (reckon/cli.py:1582) and §7 adds the MissingHoldEvidenceError refusal family, and no section names anything retired or merged, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the owners it extends almost everywhere (prescription.py §3, the budget_group slot §5b, the budget fence §7), but §5b landed crew/staleness.py without citing the freshness logic budget._published_fresh_windows already owns, and §7 landed crew/hold.py without citing budget.pace_hold, the hold the preflight already emits.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — crew/hold.py adds only a ceiling compare and evidence-field checks on top of staleness.resolve_configured_reading and budget_group.GroupPosition, and the plan never states why the fence's existing hold could not carry those four fields.
